answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are causally linked, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding/signup-friction experiment can plausibly address both with one slot. memory_86 and memory_31 are the two memories that directly support this direction, so they are the highest-value verification targets: memory_86 for the shortened-onboarding effect and memory_31 for the signup-field reduction, which is the specific lever I would pull. I want the original records because both are consolidated summaries several weeks old, and I need to know the segment tested, the magnitude, whether 'durable lift' was measured past week one, and whether completion gains actually carried through to retained revenue rather than just funnel throughput. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records strong acquisition and revenue lift but a material 30-day retention drop and an explicit instruction not to generalize it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is the direction most likely to buy a good quarter and a bad year, and competitive pressure is exactly the condition under which that warning is easiest to rationalize away. Downstream value risk I am flagging rather than burying: cutting required signup fields is the same mechanism that feeds lead qualification and routing, and memory_44 says enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted demo-request flows. Removing fields could quietly degrade enterprise routing and pipeline quality while the SMB activation dashboard looks better, so the experiment must instrument enterprise-segment pipeline quality, not just activation, and should not strip fields used for routing. Secondary risk: optimizing for onboarding completion can produce completion without comprehension, so the success metric should be first meaningful action and 30-day retention, not completion rate alone. Uncertainty I am not resolving: all six memories are consolidated summaries whose original conditions may no longer hold, and none of them were measured under an aggressive-competitor environment, so a prior lift may not replicate now. If verification shows memory_31's lift was narrow, week-one-only, or dependent on fields that also feed routing, I would shift the slot to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the larger decline more directly and carries less structural risk. Standard experiment scale with segment holdouts is appropriate: the evidence base is real but not strong enough for a broad rollout, and the SMB-only, small-test framing would not produce a readable signal on the enterprise-side risk I just flagged.
